body_presentation.source_prefix:
THEATRE REVIEW POWER PLAY or RACE TO OBLIVION

Friday, September 25, 1992

ROBERT CUSHMAN

Toronto ONT -- WRITTEN BY MARTIN HUNTER Directed by Richard Monette Starring Peter Boretski, Albert Millaire and Goldie Semple At the Tarragon Theatre Rating: Intended as an excoriating satire on devious government, Power Play is presented by something calling itself Mulroney Productions. The title of course is a pun, the power both political and nuclear, the play both drama and game Flying blind to Rio BY ROBERT CUSHMAN Special to The Globe and Mail Toronto TO begin with a detail: a Cabinet Minister glowers at his aide and asks, What's this cable from our ambassador in Rio supposed to mean? Since the fellow has just handed him the wire, he hardly needs to be told who sent it. The information is included purely for our benefit, and it seems ungrateful to complain. Ungrateful but necessary: as conversation that line is unbelievable and hence unplayable.
